---
title: "DPprior Explorer"
subtitle: "Interactive visualizations for design-conditional prior elicitation in Dirichlet process mixtures"
toc: false
---

This site is a pool of interactive visualizations built around
*Design-Conditional Prior Elicitation for Dirichlet Process Mixtures*
(Lee, 2026, [arXiv:2602.06301](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06301)).
It assumes no prior knowledge of Dirichlet process mixtures (DPMs). Its numbers come by two
routes. Prior quantities for any Gamma(a, b) or fixed alpha (cluster counts, weight tails,
calibrations, the default-method solvers) are computed in your browser by one JavaScript
engine, which is compared with the DPprior R package (version 2.0.0) and with independent R
integrals. Posterior, simulation and application results are read from released summary
tables of the replication package and never recomputed. [How the numbers are
checked](#how-the-numbers-are-checked) says what each check covers.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Where to start.** Three [learning paths](learning-paths.qmd): 25 minutes for beginners,
45 for researchers, 90 for a course, each step with its setting and what to notice. The
[catalog](catalog.qmd) lists all 72 visualizations and filters them by section, ladder rung and
audience.
:::

## The storyline

1. **[Learn the DPM](pages/dpm/index.qmd).** Following Broderick's MLSS 2016 ladder:
   why a nonparametric prior, Beta and Dirichlet weights, many components and few
   clusters, stick-breaking (GEM), the Chinese restaurant process, and the DP mixture.
2. **[The CRP bridge](pages/bridge/index.qmd).** One concentration parameter alpha sets
   both how many tables open among J units (the *count view*, K_J) and how large the
   tables are (the *weight view*, W_SB). A Gamma(a, b) hyperprior on alpha is read in the
   same table-and-stick language.
3. **[What default hyperpriors imply](pages/problems/index.qmd).** A "vague" default
   says different things at different J ([same default, different J](pages/problems/defaults-drift.qmd));
   a prior calibrated to "about five clusters" can still put a random unit in a majority
   cluster with probability .49 ([the unintended prior](pages/problems/unintended-prior.qmd)).
4. **[The DPprior principle](pages/dpprior/index.qmd).** State a design-conditional
   target, calibrate Gamma(a, b) to it (TSMM), diagnose the implied weights, and decide
   whether a Dual-Anchor adjustment is needed.
5. **[Evidence](pages/applications/index.qmd).** Simulation and three applications:
   STAR (J = 79 schools), Bangert-Drowns (J = 48 studies) and a vocabulary checklist
   (N = 500 respondents), drawn only from released summaries.

Terms are defined on the [vocabulary](pages/vocabulary.qmd) page.

## Start here

- [**Same default, different J**](pages/problems/defaults-drift.qmd) (M-01, M-02):
  Gamma(1, 1) implies 4.16 clusters at J = 50 and 7.82 at J = 2000, with the same .591
  majority-mass tail at every J.
- [**The unintended prior**](pages/problems/unintended-prior.qmd) (M-03): "about five
  clusters" and a .49 chance of majority dominance, from one hyperprior.

## How the numbers are checked

| Route | What | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Computed in your browser | prior quantities for any Gamma(a, b) or fixed alpha | compared with golden values from the DPprior R package (version 2.0.0) and with R integrals that share no code with the engine: 17,351 comparisons in 147 groups, 0 failures |
| Read from released tables | posterior, simulation and application results in 20 released tables (1.30 MB) | source, rows, columns and checksum of every table; no individual-level fields |
| Shown on the pages | the numbers the widgets and pages display | 117 displayed numbers in 28 cases on 20 widgets and 2 site pages against the R values and the released tables; six paper cross-checks of the released tables |

These checks cover the listed rows and values, not every number on every page. The released
tables are copied from the replication package, not re-derived here, and posterior fits are
never rerun. The golden values, the checks and their tolerances are in the source repository
(`verification/`, `r-export/` and `CONTRACT.md`).

## About

Built by JoonHo Lee (jlee296@ua.edu), The University of Alabama, with support from the Institute of
Education Sciences (R305D240078). Teaching material after Broderick is re-drawn from the
mathematics and attributed on each page. The DPprior R package, the replication package
and the DPprior Studio app are linked from the paper. This is release 1.1.0 (28 September 2026); the changelog in the
[source repository](https://github.com/joonho112/dpprior-explorer) lists what changed.
